title: Kernel of the unit on one stalk
statement: Let i:Z -> Y be a closed immersion [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], F an O_Y-module, x a point of Y, eta the unit of the chosen tensor pullback adjunction [def-pc-module-pullback], and J=i.ker [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. For the multiplication mu:J tensor F -> F [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], take stalks using [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. Then range(mu_x)=ker(eta_x) as submodules of F_x. This concerns the multiplication map itself, not the categorical image inclusion or a kernel universal property.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 08KS (lemma-i-star-equivalence), stalkwise argument; Sheaves, Lemmas 0098 and 00AE. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08KS because the literature checkout is not present on this machine.

proof.text: Off i(Z), the target stalk is zero. On the affine neighbourhood basis disjoint from i(Z), the ideal of i.ker is the kernel of a map to the zero ring, hence is the whole ring. range_toModulesι_app identifies it with the range of J sections. A germ of 1 in J multiplies every F germ to itself, so range(mu_x)=F_x=ker(eta_x).

At x=i(z), write R=O_Y,x, S=O_Z,z and K=ker(R -> S). The closed immersion makes the ring map surjective. On the affine basis the ideal sections are exactly the kernel of this map. Passing to stalks identifies the range of J_x -> R with K by stalk exactness. The tensor multiplication stalk range formula identifies range(mu_x) with K F_x.

The canonical unit stalk becomes m |-> 1 tensor m after the pullback and closed-pushforward stalk comparisons. Since S=R/K, TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul identifies S tensor_R F_x with F_x/(K F_x), compatibly with this map. Equivalently the inverse sends r-bar tensor m to r*m modulo K F_x: changing a lift changes r*m by K F_x, and the balanced relation is respected. Thus ker(eta_x)=K F_x.

For the chosen adjunction, the unit differs from the canonical unit by postcomposition with the pushforward of a natural isomorphism of left adjoints. Its stalk map is invertible, so postcomposition preserves the kernel.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 08KS, with the explicit local tensor quotient calculation and adjunction transport written out.

lean.statement:
theorem closedImmersion_unit_stalk_kernel {Y Z : Scheme.{w}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (F : Y.Modules) (x : Y) :
    let adj := Classical.choice (nonempty_tensorPullbackAdjunction i)
    let J : Y.IdealSheafData := i.ker
    let μ : J.toModules ⊗ F ⟶ F := J.toModulesι ▷ F ≫ (λ_ F).hom
    let S := RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y.toRingedSpace x
    LinearMap.range (S.map μ).hom = LinearMap.ker (S.map (adj.unit.app F)).hom
